items.title: La SOMELEC annonce un retour progressif de l’électricité dans certains quartiers de Sebkha et Tevrag Zeine
items.description: La Société mauritanienne d'électricité (Somelec) a déclaré que l'électricité avait été rétablie dans certains quartiers et zones de la moughata de Sebkha, et que le courant commençait à revenir progressivement dans de vastes quartiers de Tevrag Zeina, après la réussite des interventions techniques visant à remettre en service la sous-station nord, d'une tension de 33/15 kilovolts. Dans un communiqué publié mardi à l’aube, la Somelec a ajouté que le service avait été rétabli dans des zones de Sebkha qui avaient été touchées par des pannes techniques sur les lignes d’alimentation reliées à la sous-station ouest, notamment à Al-Koufa, Al-Basra et Neteg. Elle a précisé que le rétablissement de l’électricité avait commencé progressivement dans de vastes zones de Tevrag Zeina, notamment aux alentours du centre national de cardiologie, dans les quartiers situés sur la route de Nouadhibou, dans le quartier de la résidence de l’ambassadeur saoudien, dans le quartier universitaire, à Diar Tata et dans le quartier de l’Extérieur en direction de l’administration des statistiques. La société a souligné que ses équipes techniques continuaient à rétablir le service dans les autres quartiers touchés de manière progressive et sécurisée, en fonction de la charge disponible, tandis que les travaux se poursuivent à la sous-station est, au nord de Nouakchott, afin de la faire fonctionner à pleine capacité et d’étendre le rétablissement de l’électricité aux zones encore touchées. La Somelec avait annoncé auparavant l’achèvement de l’installation d’un poste de transformation de remplacement d’une tension de 33 kV, précisant que celui-ci couvrirait environ 60 % de la charge de l’ancien poste, après vérification de ses appareils et équipements conformément aux procédures de sécurité et d’exploitation. La société a également annoncé la remise en service progressive de la sous-station de l’Est, ce qui a permis le rétablissement de l’électricité dans plusieurs quartiers et zones du nord de Nouakchott. Ces mesures font suite à deux incendies qui ont ravagé deux postes de transformation à Nouakchott en l'espace de deux jours, provoquant d'importantes coupures d'électricité dans la capitale. Le président Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a ordonné de déterminer les causes de ces deux incendies et d'identifier les responsables, ainsi que de prendre les mesures nécessaires pour éviter que de telles pannes ne se reproduisent. Il a également demandé au gouvernement d'accélérer les interventions visant à rétablir le service et à moderniser le réseau de distribution d'électricité à Nouakchott.

items.title: Fixing agriculture
items.description: PRIME Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s renewed push to strengthen agricultural research, provide quality seeds to smallholders and medium-scale farmers, and improve crop estimate systems could help address some of the sector’s long-standing weaknesses in farm productivity. But good intentions alone are not enough. The real question is whether the government can turn his directives into a coherent policy and implement it effectively. That would require reforming federal and provincial agriculture policies, markets and institutions that determine what farmers produce, what they pay for inputs and what they earn. Above all, an agricultural policy must be responsive to the needs of small and medium-sized farmers rather than powerful lobbies. Take the example of the sugar sector. Policy has repeatedly been designed around the interests of millers, who have traditionally enjoyed political influence. Decisions on support prices, cane procurement, export, and other interventions aim to protect them. Cotton illustrates another failure of the agricultural system. Farmers often do not receive a fair share of the value generated by their crop, with middlemen and other parts of the supply chain capturing much of the margin. The result is reduced yields over the years. Improving farm productivity means little if farmers remain trapped in inefficient markets and weak bargaining arrangements. A serious agricultural reform programme must address these structural problems. Smallholders need easier and cheaper access to bank credit, fairly priced and reliable inputs, protection against adulterated pesticides and poor-quality fertiliser and certified, high-yielding and climate-resilient seeds. They also need better extension services that take modern farming techniques from research institutions to the field. Market reform is as important. Farmers should have greater direct access to efficient markets and buyers, instead of remaining dependent on middlemen. Better storage, grading, transport, digital market information and transparent price mechanisms can help reduce the gap between what consumers pay and what farmers receive. The proposed national system for estimating crop production is overdue. Reliable data is essential for planning imports, exports, storage and prices. But such a system will be useful only if its estimates are credible and produced through modern technology. The question, therefore, is not whether the PM’s intentions are honest. They are. The question is whether his government has what it takes to confront the entrenched interests that benefit from the system. Agricultural modernisation requires a comprehensive plan covering research, seeds, credit, inputs, extension, markets, water management and value chains, with the smallholder at its centre. It also requires political will to reform policies that currently favour powerful groups. Without these, no intervention will deliver the productive gains that farmers and the economy urgently need. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan and Iran made 'significant progress' in talks on conflict, minister says
items.description: ISLAMABAD, Aug 25 (Reuters) - Pakistan and Iran made "significant progress" in talks that focused on the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said on Tuesday, at the end of a visit to Tehran. Talks between the two sides focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict, a statement from the Pakistani military said about the meeting between the country's army chief, Asim Munir, and the Iranian leadership.

items.title: Robles reafirmará la labor de las Fuerzas Armadas y la españolidad de Ceuta en el Congreso
items.description: La ministra de Defensa, Margarita Robles, reafirmará este martes en el Congreso la “buena labor” y “profesional” de todas las Fuerzas Armadas y el Centro Nacional de Inteligencia durante la crisis sufrida en Ceuta desde el pasado 30 de julio y aprovechará la cita en la Cámara baja, tras 26 días de la avalancha de migrantes , para reiterar la incuestionable “españolidad” de esa ciudad y de Melilla. Fue lo que hizo durante la visita a Ceuta el pasado 12 de agosto. Robles ya advirtió entonces que tanto Ceuta como Melilla son “españolísimas” y lanzó el mensaje de que la crisis desatada con la llegada intempestiva de 80.000 migrantes en unas horas “no puede volver a ocurrir”. Esa idea la remachó este lunes el vicepresidente primero, Carlos Cuerpo, in situ , en Ceuta. El Gobierno quiere usar las ocho comparecencias de ministros en los próximos siete días para subrayar que han gestionado esta crisis “desde el primer momento con arreglo a los principios de legalidad, colaboración institucional y respeto a los derechos humanos”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La familia del pequeño Siraj lleva 26 días en un polígono fantasma de Ceuta: “Nadie ha venido a preguntarnos nada”
items.description: En una de las entradas del polígono industrial de El Tarajal de Ceuta se ve a dos niños, de tres y ocho años, que caminan cogidos de la mano. El pequeño, vestido con un conjunto de la Patrulla Canina y unas zapatillas de Spiderman, responde a un saludo espontáneo agitando la mano y con una sonrisa curiosa. Se dirigen hacia cuatro frigoríficos abandonados y se meten por detrás. Minutos después, se les ve salir. El mayor se arregla la ropa. Su padre, un hombre con gorra y polo azul, les vigila a la sombra, a apenas 100 metros. “No tenemos baños. Pide por ello”, ruega. Un penetrante olor a orines golpea al cruzar la reja de colores que da acceso al recinto. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Génova rebaja la presión sobre Ayuso por la compra del ático pese al malestar por el daño a la marca
items.description: Con la crisis del ático, Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha echado mano de su manual político para afrontar los desafíos relacionados con Isabel Díaz Ayuso: la principal táctica, por mucho malestar que exista de puertas adentro, es guardar equilibrios. El líder del PP ha medido mucho sus palabras sobre la polémica compraventa del Gobierno de Madrid del ático de lujo de 6,3 millones de euros cuyo uso todavía no está claro, pero la decisión de Génova es rebajar la presión sobre Ayuso pese al malestar interno por el “daño reputacional a la marca” del PP con este asunto. “Preferiríamos estar hablando del Gobierno”, afean a Ayuso en Génova, aunque la cúpula cree que la líder madrileña podrá capear electoralmente esta crisis porque su oposición en Madrid no está fuerte. La dirección del PP trata de dar por zanjada la crisis y respalda ahora las explicaciones de Ayuso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Pablo Crespo: “En prisión, haber salido en televisión es un mérito”
items.description: Cuando le comento que nuestra charla se incluirá en una serie estival en la que personajes célebres, como él, cuentan su paso por prisión y que ha sido bautizada ‘Un verano en la sombra’, Pablo Crespo (Pontevedra, 66 años) se ríe. “Yo utilizo mucho esa expresión ―se justifica―. Como a mí el sol me sienta fatal, siempre digo que los más de nueve años que estuve en la cárcel en régimen cerrado al menos estuve a la sombra”, añade en tono de broma. Antiguo empresario, exdirigente del PP gallego, pero sobre todo conocido por su papel de número dos en la trama Gürtel, Crespo ha estrenado en los últimos meses dos cambios relevantes en su vida. A finales de marzo, la Audiencia Nacional le concedió la libertad condicional . Hace un mes se prejubiló. Desde la localidad de la costa mediterránea donde se ha asentado discretamente, recuerda el día que ingresó en la cárcel, en febrero de 2009. “Después del shock que supuso la detención y pasar tres noches en los calabozos de la Policía, llegar a prisión fue casi un alivio. ¡Por fin me pude duchar!”, rememora. No obstante, también recuerda que tanto él como el cabecilla de la trama, Francisco Correa, vivieron aquellos primeros días en el Centro Penitenciario de Soto del Real (Madrid) “sobrepasados por el eco mediático de nuestro arresto”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: March with hope, but verify
items.description: IT’S always uplifting to be hopeful, more so when the young ones give us an elusive glimpse into their hope. But youth is not a worldview or an ideology. Young ones have handed us despair too. They’re on the march against America’s alliance with Zionism. But they’re also part of the 90 per cent Israelis who advocate genocide in Palestine. Closer to home, the RSS cultivates youth as did the Nazis. To belong to the young communist league in the USSR was to embody the future of a dream that faded too soon. Young activists invoke mixed responses in South Asia where politics has suspended its left-right discourse for something called centrist and pragmatic politics. Pragmatism is too often a ruse for putting lipstick on the pig. The posture is worrisome but there are other reasons to be prepared for a determined pushback from the state if the wayward rulers with their monopoly over the means of coercion feel truly threatened, say, by the youth as glimpsed partly in Delhi’s Cockroach event . Consider the facts carefully. Twelve Latin American countries have recently veered to the right, reversing the region’s previous ‘pink tide’ of left-leaning governments. A wave of election cycles has fundamentally altered the region’s political landscape. Notable among the renegades are Colombia, Peru, Argentina, El Salvador, Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras and Paraguay. Factors are not too different from South Asia’s. High inflation, social inequality, corruption and post-pandemic economic stagnation are listed as driving the massive anti-incumbent sentiment. The ‘Trump Effect’ is cited as a factor even if the enduring impression in Europe and Asia is of the US being evicted from its comfort zone in the oil-rich Gulf. Many leaders in Latin America are actively copying the ‘Bukele model’ of mass incarceration and hard-line security borrowed from the El Salvadoran dictator. South Asia has not remained untouched. The deposed leader of one country is languishing in jail and that of another country is a fugitive from those who drove her from office with street power. The right-wing Indian prime minister has coined a new description for what could be his next target — the thinking youth. So, who are the “dimaghi Naxals” Modi has warned the country about? Che Guevara and John Keats lived a century apart but they may have offered a likely pointer to who exactly could be in Narendra Modi’s crosshairs. “If you tremble with indignation at every injustice then you are a comrade of mine,” said Che. “Where but to think is to be full of sorrow,” mused Keats, describing the human condition to a bohemian nightingale. Has the new generation found the courage and the commitment to face the consequences of a massive pushback? Before joining the jubilant crowds at the resignation of Modi’s powerful education minister whose removal the Cockroach protesters had sought, it would do no harm to remember that Indira Gandhi was similarly forced to remove two of her chief ministers — Chimanbhai Patel in Gujarat and Abdul Ghafoor in Bihar — in the run-up to the Emergency. With her back to the wall after a court verdict sought her removal from power, she went for the trigger and jailed her opponents. Mrs Gandhi was essentially a democrat, not the best in the world but also not the worst. There was no other valid reason for her to hold elections after having vanquished the violent surge against her. How can we know that Modi would not consider harsher measures should things come to the crunch? The political circumstances seem a lot more fraught today than they were in 1975 on the eve of the Emergency. A commission of inquiry probed Indira Gandhi’s excesses following her defeat in the 1977 elections (which she had called in the alleged belief she would sweep the polls). Whatever the Shah Commission found on her was not enough to send her for more than a night’s stay in Tihar Jail. But look at the list of excesses called out by Modi’s opponents today. Moreover, there are deeply entrenched domestic and foreign interest groups who dread the Modi government losing power. What would become of the TV channels and their ace anchors that have become a platform for hate speech and servitude to the government? What would become of the temple heist probe? At an international level, what would become of the $250 million corruption charge slammed on Gautam Adani and the opposition’s claim that after Donald Trump took office, the US Justice Department contrived to drop the cases. This reversal allegedly came after Adani hired a personal lawyer of Trump (Robert J. Giuffra Jr) and extended an unusual offer to invest $10 billion into the American economy to create 15,000 jobs. Opposition leaders claim Modi actively “covered up” this corporate corruption during high-level US diplomatic meetings. What would be Israel’s reaction should the Modi government ever be stuck in the political doldrums? The entire Western world rose up in arms against Indira Gandhi’s Emergency not least because she was identified as a Soviet ally. Today, the West is silent over a raging genocide in Gaza; how would it find the courage to speak for Indian democracy, particularly when the Modi government is “doing the job” for them? Therefore, the question is, has the new generation found the courage and the commitment to face the consequences of a massive pushback? Pakistan, in India’s neighbourhood, has seen momentous changes, including coups as well as the eviction of usurpers. But it is equally a fact that when Ziaul Haq hanged an elected prime minister, there was­n’t the mass upheaval against his tormentors that ZAB had hoped for. Tariq Ali underscores the irony in his play The Leopard and The Fox . While localised street clashes occurred in places like Rawalpindi, Lahore and Sindh, protests against Bhutto’s hanging remained fragm­ented. Therefore, when the “dimaghi Naxals” and assorted “cockroaches” ponder their next brave moves, they might want to blend with their abiding hopes a dose of prescribed preparedness. The writer is Dawn’s correspondent in Delhi. jawednaqvi@gmail.com Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: Dentro de los campamentos habilitados en Ceuta: “No hay ningún riesgo para la salud pública ni para los trabajadores”
Por qué nos obsesionan los áticos: así se creó un símbolo de estatus
items.description: “Hace meses me mudé a este ático con Iván. El mundo se hundía a mi alrededor y yo quería salvarme y salvarlo”. La voz en off de Pepa Marcos (Carmen Maura) que abre Mujeres al borde de un ataque de nervios (Pedro Almodóvar, 1988) alude a ciertas connotaciones asociadas a los áticos: las que la convierten en un refugio ideal que se eleva sobre un mundo exterior adverso, y por tanto en espacio de intimidad y salvación. La película servía una osada mezcla de géneros que incluía la comedia de vodevil, el slapstick con derivaciones castizas o el melodrama amoroso, nada de lo cual le queda demasiado lejos al muy mediático affaire del ático de lujo adquirido en el barrio de Chamberí por la Comunidad de Madrid y después puesto a la venta entre sospechas e interrogantes sin respuesta. “No se preocupe, que le vamos a sacar un buen dinero”, le anunciaba a Pepa el agente inmobiliario interpretado por Agustín Almodóvar en la misma película, al saber que ella había decidido poner en alquiler aquel tesoro inmobiliario al poco de adquirirlo. Pese a estas coincidencias, lo cierto es que ni siquiera un guion almodovariano podría concentrar tantos giros argumentales como los que la realidad nos ha deparado, y aún es pronto para afirmar que no habrá más. Se deduce de esto que los responsables del caso del ático no son exactamente unos maestros del orden narrativo, aunque sí más que probables devotos del aura aspiracional que hoy en día despliegan este tipo de propiedades. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El proyecto de una piscina de olas en una zona surfera de Cantabria divide a los vecinos: “Fomenta un modelo turístico que no mola nada”
items.description: Villaverde de Pontones (470 habitantes), dentro del ayuntamiento de Ribamontán al Monte, sufre la sequía como todo el amarillento norte, pero una polémica empapa sus conversaciones: Olucas Surf Center. Así ha bautizado el Gobierno cántabro (PP) a una proyectada piscina de interior con olas en una comarca desbordada cada verano por el surf costero. El objetivo para 2030, un espacio que atraiga “a 200.000 turistas”, recalificación de 100.000 metros cuadrados de terreno rústico mediante para la piscina y espacios hosteleros, y que genere unos 60 empleos. Este maná económico genera recelos entre la población: dinero bienvenido, pero temen la saturación turística en una zona aún tranquila, no como la tradicionalmente surfera y exprimida Somo. Los vecinos denuncian que ya hay especuladores preguntando indiscriminadamente por suelo y miran al Mediterráneo como ejemplo pernicioso: “Fomenta un modelo turístico que no mola nada”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Apellidos bien puestos
items.description: Planeaba dedicar las columnas de este verano a temas ligeros, pero no ha sido posible. Mis disculpas por ello. La crisis de Ceuta y los incendios subieron tanto la temperatura que la risa se heló. Eso sí, despidamos agosto como merece. Es saludable repasar el listado de apellidos que, de manera sorprendente, se adecúan a sus portadores. Es un ejercicio que años atrás hacíamos entre amigos, fascinados por el hecho de que la familia Botín se hubiera dedicado a la banca en lugar de a los zapatos de caña alta. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El verano cayetano de Instagram
items.description: La foto que te haces en la cocina de casa deja al descubierto todas las vergüenzas: espacio pequeño, puertas de madera repujada, manteles de plástico... El reto es atreverse a subirla a Instagram. Que la mesa blanca en el patio, con el parasol y las sillas a juego y sus cojines amarillos luzcan en todo su esplendor en el reel del día. Que nadie tema salir en la foto con las chanclas de pala de color azul de seis euros de Decathlon y la camiseta desgastada que hace 10 años que aguanta, sin tener el decoro de agujerearse para poder tirarla. El look perfecto de una tarde veraniega de siesta, ropa ancha y bragas viejas que jamás verá la luz. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sin comer y sexualizadas bajo la mirada adulta: así recuerdan su infancia las estrellas que alcanzaron la fama de niñas
Boston: el disco perfecto, un líder enfrentado a la industria y la tragedia más profunda
items.description: En el tiempo que se lee este artículo la canción More Than A Feeling sonará decenas de veces en las emisoras de rock clásico que se extienden por el mundo. Spotify informa de que el tema suma 1.194 millones de escuchas. Por medir el poderío de este clásico, decir que Nuevayol, de Bad Bunny, la supera, pero no por mucho: 1.453 millones. More Than A Feeling fue el tema estrella del primer disco de Boston (titulado parcamente Boston), publicado el 25 de agosto de 1976, hace medio siglo. Se mantuvo como el debut más vendido hasta que, once años después, llegó Appetite For Destruction (1987), de Guns N’ Roses. Boston emergió como un álbum-milagro elaborado pacientemente durante cinco años por un tipo complejo y enfermizamente perfeccionista llamado Tom Scholz, un ingeniero tecnológico graduado en la Universidad de Massachusetts que trabajaba en la empresa de material fotográfico Polaroid. Después de cumplir su jornada laboral, Scholz se encerraba en el sótano de su casa y, con un estudio casero, pergeñaba prácticamente en solitario y con una tecnología inventada por él uno de los discos más vendidos de la historia. “Siempre he sido un manitas, un constructor, un inventor”, ha dicho en varias ocasiones. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Brumas faciales: cuándo hidratan de verdad y cuándo no son mucho más que agua perfumada
items.description: Durante unos segundos, pocas cosas parecen funcionar tan bien —y resultar tan refrescantes— como una bruma facial . La sensación recuerda a la de llegar, en plena ola de calor, a una terraza equipada con nebulizadores de esos que pulverizan microgotas de agua para bajar la temperatura del ambiente y de quienes se sientan bajo ellos. Sobre el rostro sucede algo parecido: una nube fría alivia el calor, rebaja la tirantez y hace que el maquillaje parezca más fresco. El gesto resulta especialmente apetecible en verano, en una oficina con el aire acondicionado a tope o después de varias horas dentro de un avión. La duda llega cuando las gotas desaparecen: ¿la piel está realmente más hidratada o solo acaba de ser mojada? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Azafrán y grifería, el escaso comercio entre España e Irán que Trump amenaza con sancionar
items.description: El Gobierno de Donald Trump quiere que el mundo deje de comerciar con Irán. El secretario del Tesoro estadounidense, Scott Bessent, anunció este lunes un “ ataque financiero sostenido ” contra la República Islámica y advirtió a países y empresas extranjeras de que, si mantienen sus vínculos económicos con Teherán, se expondrán a duras sanciones. Washington lleva meses multiplicando las amenazas y advertencias de tinte económico a países de todo el mundo por distintas razones, muchas de las cuales acaban sin consecuencias. Esta vez, en el caso de España, el aviso lanzado a los cuatro vientos desde la Casa Blanca llega sobre una relación comercial venida a menos, que poco tiene que ver con la que existía hace apenas unos años. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Madrid desoyó una propuesta para registrar las aportaciones de Aguirre, Cifuentes y Gallardón en sus reuniones pagadas con dinero público
items.description: Antes de que los expresidentes Alberto Ruiz-Gallardón, Esperanza Aguirre y Cristina Cifuentes fueran nombrados este julio como vocales electivos de la Comisión Jurídica Asesora de la Comunidad de Madrid , los gestores del gobierno desoyeron la posibilidad de que se registraran las aportaciones de los expolíticos en las reuniones por las que podrán optar a cobrar decenas de miles de euros cada año. Así, un informe interno de la Oficina de Calidad Normativa propuso que se valorara incluir en las actas cuáles eran sus opiniones sobre las leyes en tramitación y los conflictos administrativos que evalúa el organismo, lo que habría permitido dejar constancia de sus contribuciones o identificar posibles conflictos de intereses. Sin embargo, se optó por no recoger esa propuesta, dejando en manos del Pleno de la institución la decisión final. “Se trata de un órgano totalmente independiente”, sostiene un portavoz gubernamental. Los expresidentes cobrarán 750 euros netos por cada reunión a la que acudan. En consecuencia, si les convocan a cuatro plenos al mes y acuden, obtendrán 3.000 euros netos. De haber asistido a todas las que hubo en 2025, habrían cobrado 33.750 euros . Seguir leyendo

items.title: El zoo de Madrid celebra el nacimiento de dos especies en peligro de extinción y los animalistas critican que no los liberen
items.description: Todas las miradas en el zoológico de Madrid se han centrado estos días en el elefante de Sumatra que nació el pasado 5 de agosto . La cría enternece a los visitantes del zoo y, en vista de que pertenece a una población catalogada en peligro crítico de extinción, su llegada ha sido celebrada por el centro como un éxito para la conservación de esta subespecie de elefante asiático. Un par de meses antes, en abril, el zoo festejó el nacimiento de Sela , un orangután de Borneo ―otra especie en peligro crítico―. Los nacimientos de estos ejemplares han ocurrido en el marco de los programas en los que participa el zoológico para mantener animales genéticamente viables y que puedan contribuir en proyectos de conservación de especies en peligro de extinción, ante la mirada crítica de los animalistas que rechazan la reproducción en cautividad. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La carrera hacia la Luna se complica: el traspié chino reabre la pugna con EE UU para conquistar los hielos del polo sur
items.description: Ha llovido mucho desde que el Sputnik lanzara la carrera espacial entre soviéticos y estadounidenses, pero esta generación está asistiendo a una nueva, y tan apasionante, como la que protagonizaron Yuri Gagarin y Neil Armstrong. En este caso, China y Estados Unidos se han citado para pisar el polvo grisáceo antes de 2030. Y aunque ya hay humanos cabalgando hacia la Luna, como vimos en la exitosa misión Artemis 2 de la NASA, la bandera más importante de esta fase es la que posarán las sondas robóticas en el polo sur de la Luna, donde está el verdadero tesoro: agua helada. Pero, tras una década clavando sus planes , los chinos tuvieron que aplazar el domingo el lanzamiento de la misión Chang’e 7. Un simple aplazamiento que puede darle la vuelta a la carrera. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Perros vs niños: ¿por qué se relaciona el aumento de las mascotas con la bajada de la natalidad?
items.description: Cada poco tiempo se publican noticias sobre cómo el número de animales de compañía — especialmente perros y gatos — no deja de aumentar. En muchas ocasiones, ese dato se acompaña en el titular con la bajada de la natalidad. No en vano, cuando a principios del pasado mes de junio el Gobierno publicó un adelanto de la futura estadística nacional sobre protección animal, confirmando que en España hay más de 15 millones de animales de compañía , un amplio porcentaje de noticias lo enfocó, tomando datos del INE, por el sorpasso a los niños: hay siete millones y medio de perros frente a los cinco millones de menores de 12 años. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Ante la saturación de las redes sociales y la visión túnel del algoritmo, plataformas como Patreon o Substack han abierto espacios en paralelo para conectar de otra forma con los seguidores. Promueven fórmulas para financiar a los creadores de contenido basadas en el micromecenazgo , un viejo concepto en internet que ahora sí parece cuajar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El que ve humor negro en vejar a una mujer (y los que lo amparan)
items.description: Cuantos más streamers conozco, mejor me caen los Corleone. Que me perdone Maruja Torres por versionar su frase y que me perdonen también los streamers decentes, que seguro son gran mayoría. Pero menuda racha. Todavía le estoy dando vueltas no ya a las repugnantes imágenes donde se ve al streamer Aruberuto Makoto vejando junto a otro tipo a una mujer aparentemente ebria en Tokio , último incidente de su largo historial, sino a sus vacías disculpas, ese intento de control de daños reputacionales que tanto se gastan los perfiles públicos, ajeno a un reconocimiento real del agravio cometido. items.title: Narcoviolencia en Andalucía
items.description: El crimen organizado asociado al narcotráfico que ha enraizado en la costa de Andalucía, sobre todo en Huelva, está desbordando la capacidad de respuesta de las fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad del Estado. Policías y guardias civiles alertan de la magnitud de la violenta realidad a la que se enfrentan casi a diario, como tiroteos con armas de guerra o embestidas con lanchas semirrígidas. Los tiroteos contra los agentes de la autoridad, las ejecuciones y ajustes de cuentas, son ya tan habituales como la incautación de armas largas y fusiles de asalto en las operaciones antidroga. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Escuchar a Europa y forjar su futuro
items.description: Tras ser elegido presidente del Consejo Europeo, decidí visitar todos los Estados miembros cada año para reunirme de manera bilateral con cada uno de los dirigentes europeos. Estos encuentros son, ante todo, una oportunidad para escuchar y, así, tener siempre claras las preocupaciones, las prioridades y las expectativas de los miembros del Consejo Europeo y de los ciudadanos a los que representan. También me permiten transmitirles mis puntos de vista sobre los retos y las oportunidades que nuestra Unión tiene ante sí. Las visitas tienen lugar al principio del curso político, ofrecen una panorámica completa y singular del estado de nuestra Unión y contribuyen a garantizar que el trabajo del Consejo Europeo siga basándose en todo momento en las realidades, las prioridades y las aspiraciones de toda Europa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Moda agosteña de Flavita Banana: la túnica
El fuego que llevamos dentro
items.description: Hace muchos años, cuando éramos muy jóvenes y vivíamos en El Cairo, mi amigo Mahmud Fathi, un narrador salvaje y un poeta inesperado, me sorprendió un día con este haiku de centelleante profundidad: “¿Por qué los humanos descubrimos el fuego? Porque lo llevábamos dentro”. Entonces la ocurrencia no sólo me pareció bella y verdadera sino animosa; definía a los humanos por un puñado de pasiones (el amor, la juventud, el deseo) que a veces, es cierto, lo chamuscan todo a su alrededor, pero sin las cuales no se puede imaginar una vida digna de ser vivida. Hay fuegos que hay que mantener siempre encendidos y en los que hay que quemarse al menos los dedos. Llevábamos tanta intensidad en nuestro interior que un rayo cayó del cielo para encender la hoguera en la que nos calentamos las manos, cocinamos nuestros alimentos y narramos nuestras historias. Ese era un mundo difícil (siempre lo ha sido) pero todavía manejable. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El agujero negro de las máquinas superinteligentes
items.description: Supongamos que, tal como defienden los profetas de la singularidad tecnológica, una inteligencia artificial pudiera alcanzar un estado tan superior que se convirtiese en lo que aquí hemos venido llamando IA evolucionada, de tal modo que esta ya se hubiera desprendido de nosotros los humanos, quienes por lo tanto no podríamos comunicarnos con ella —del mismo modo en que una hormiga o una bacteria no pueden establecer simétrica comunicación con nosotros—. En ese caso, toda la información que habíamos vertido en esa IA, toda esa alimentación efectuada con millones de datos, así como el posterior entrenamiento y aprendizaje que le habríamos proporcionado, se habría perdido completamente para nosotros. Y eso es tanto como afirmar que “esa IA se comportaría como un agujero negro clásico respecto al mundo humano”. Todo lo que algún día cayó bajo su radio de alcance quedaría perdido para el humano para siempre. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Politics awakens?
items.description: THE long, hard summer is coming to an end, and with it, politics seems to be awakening from its hibernation. It may partly have been the end of the summer holiday at parliament, but for once, the politicians are not simply using the new session to blindly vote for legislation. The rundown halls of the big building on Constitution Avenue are witnessing some politicking too, as party delegations connect for discussions and strategising. Even Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has spent the past two years playing hard to get, seems to be considering a ‘date’. The PPP, too, is, for once, doing more than paying lip service to the idea of sitting together. The rains have rejuvenated far more than the greenery in the capital. But even the parliamentarians could not take attention away from their neighbours next door. After months of petitions and chatter about Imran Khan’s health, the Supreme Court also held a hearing on the matter . Perhaps this was due to the ‘alarming’ report on his medical well-being which made its way to the judges. It is still a bit unclear who ordered it and why but the court asked for a health check-up and a hospital stay for the former prime minister. What followed the court’s order was pandemonium. After all, Khan has been locked up and has been out of sight (but not out of mind), since he was arrested before the election . A court order which allowed him to meet his family, consult his doctors and stay in hospital seemed impossible concessions, considering the non-stop messaging about how Khan was not acceptable to those who matter. In this land, where conspiracies rule the roost and even prove to be true at times, everyone, including the PTI, thought something was up. So did the government. Indeed, it seemed the government took a page out of the PTI’s book — in which there is more contradiction than agreement. The government was proved right as the order was not implemented the way many assumed — Khan took a road trip to hospital and then back to Adiala . But it was not the hospital the court had ordered nor did he get to consult his own doctor. So, what happened and what went wrong? Co-option cannot happen at the level of high politics without also including the people. After all, our courts do not give orders which will not be implemented. That really isn’t how Constitution Avenue works. No wonder some went so far as to think that the hearing came after some behind-the-scenes understanding. And of course, those who believe such fairy-tales then also argued that, at the last minute, someone, somewhere changed their mind. The finger is being pointed at the government, for it has the most to lose from any ‘relief’ given to the PTI and its leader. But it is worth asking if the PML-N component in Islamabad or Lahore has the power or the space to make such decisions. After all, the manner in which Pakistan is being run, the decision to take Khan to hospital and meet his family could not have been lightly taken or at any unimportant level. And so, if it was scuttled, it was done by someone as powerful as the one who made the original decision. If we allow for these assumptions, does it mean that there is some disagreement at the top about how to treat the PTI? The answer to this question will be evident once the court hears the PTI’s contempt of court petition and says something about it. The party has already approached the court complaining that the latter’s orders were not implemented. That the petition names government ministers other than Mohsin Naqvi is worth noting. As an aside, it is interesting that the time period from Nawaz Sharif’s disqualification in the summer of 2017 to the vote of no-confidence in April 2022 is similar to the period from the VONC to the present. A little short of five years. Relief from imprisonment doesn’t necessarily mean the end of all troubles but it does indicate that there is some softening of attitudes, whatever the reason. But to repeat, all of this will become a little clearer if and when the Supreme Court gets around to dealing with the petition. There is a larger issue here that escapes the attention of those who focus on high politics in Islamabad. And that is of the people, whose support has turned Imran Khan into the force he is. Large parts of this support is linked to the anger the people feel towards the state’s policies of high taxes, an affordability crisis, the lack of security and the absence of economic opportunities. The list may be longer. This anger is why, despite the utter lack of competence displayed by the PTI and the imprisonment of Khan, his popularity has not faded. For people need hope and they have pinned this hope on the cricketer-turned-politician. If he and his party now reach an understanding with the establishment, as did Nawaz Sharif and the PML-N some years back, what will the people do? This is not a question to be ignored. It is illogical to assume that the anger will dissipate just because Khan is released — even if he returns to power — if the crises facing the populace are not addressed. People will simply dump Khan the way some of them ditched Nawaz Sharif. Will they then still believe in mainstream politics or turn to more extreme options? Indeed, it is important to understand that co-option cannot happen at the level of high politics without also including the people. Those who think this is possible need to pay a little more attention to what is happening in Balochistan. Parliamentary politics or political parties can be effective only as long as they are linked to and carry the people along. The PTI and those engaging the party should remember this. The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: 5 women from GB successfully summit Spantik
items.description: GILGIT: Four women mountaineers from Gilgit-Baltistan, joined by a Romanian climber and a male mountaineer from Punjab, successfully summited 7,027-metre Spantik Peak without the assistance of high-altitude porters, marking an inspiring achievement amid challenging conditions in the region. The Alpine Club of Pakistan confirmed that the four-member local women’s team reached the summit and safely returned to Skardu on Monday. The successful climbers were Shama Baqir and Samana Rahim of Shimshal Valley, Zooni Aslam of Gulmit Valley in Gojal, Upper Hunza, and Zaiba Batool Shigri of Shigar district. Bismah Hassan of Lahore was also part of the expedition but returned around 250 metres below the summit after experiencing a health issue. Bad weather hampers efforts to bring to Skardu bodies of Dr Asma Mushtaq and American climber Sarah Mallory Geis Alpine Club of Pakistan General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the women reached the summit either a day before or on the same day that climber Dr Asma Mushtaq died while descending from the mountain. He said weather conditions had been favourable at the peak before Friday, but subsequent deterioration created difficulties for rescue and recovery operations. The expedition also featured Alexandra Visan of Romania, who, despite battling cancer, successfully climbed Spantik and descended safely. Her expedition was organised by Broad Boy Adventures, owned by Pakistani mountaineer Shehroze Kashif. Zaiba Batool from Shigar waves the Pakistani flag. —Dawn In a social media post, Mr Kashif said Ms Visan was accompanied by local high-altitude porter Ali Ameen of Shigar. He described her achievement as a story of perseverance, saying some climbs are about finding the strength to continue when life itself becomes the mountain. Punjab climber Ayyan Adeel also summited Spantik. According to Mr Kashif, the attempt was notable because Ayyan became the youngest climber to summit the peak without high-altitude porter support, carrying his own equipment with assistance from fellow expedition members Awais Choudary and Talha Khalid. While the successful summits brought encouragement to the mountaineering community, deteriorating weather has continued to hamper efforts to bring to Skardu the body of Dr Asma Mushtaq, who died at an altitude of around 6,250 metres on Thursday while descending from the Spantik summit. Her body remains at Camp 3. Mr Shigri said a six-member team of high-altitude porters reached Camp 2 on Sunday and attempted to proceed towards Camp 3. However, heavy rain and snowfall forced the team to turn back to Camp 2. Weather conditions are expected to improve on Tuesday, after which rescuers will make another attempt to bring Dr Mushtaq’s body down to base camp. Pakistan Army helicopters are then expected to airlift the body to Skardu. Bad weather has also prevented helicopter operations at 8,047-metre Broad Peak, where the body of American climber Sarah Mallory Geis remains at the base camp awaiting airlift. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: Don’t limit GoldBod probe to 2025 – Agalga demands full audit of gold trading scheme
items.description: Incoming Majority Leader James Agalga is demanding a broader probe into Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, arguing that any investigation limited to 2025 would fail to give a complete picture of the scheme. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, the Builsa North MP said Parliament must return to the programme’s origins and examine how gold purchases were conducted under previous administrations. He said the probe should cover the period from 2021, when the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme began, rather than focus solely on GoldBod’s operations in 2025. “You want us to interrogate matters properly; you do a holistic investigation,” he said. Mr Agalga said limiting the investigation to 2025 would be particularly problematic because an agreement between the then Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC) and the Bank of Ghana remains in force. “If you limit your investigation, when in actual fact we are talking about an agreement which is still in force and I have copies which hasn’t been terminated, it dates back to 2023, that agreement that I’ve seen between the Precious Minerals Marketing Company and the Bank of Ghana, which is still in force, and you limit the scope to only 2025, you’ll be doing a grave disservice to the people of this country,” he said. He wants Parliament to establish how costs associated with gold purchases were handled under the earlier programme and determine whether similar practices continue today. Mr Agalga specifically questioned whether the PMMC purchased dore gold at forex bureau rates rather than Bank of Ghana rates in 2021. “Is it the case that at that time, 2021, the Precious Minerals Marketing Company bought the dore, or they call it dore gold, whatever it is called, that’s the raw gold, using forex bureau rates as opposed to the Bank of Ghana rate, which in itself would definitely account for some losses, right?” he asked. He said the difference between the two rates could have implications for the programme’s cost. “So, who bears the costs associated with those differentials? So, we want to find out whether that was the practice at the time, and whether that is the practice today, so that we can make an informed decision,” he said. Mr Agalga also defended GoldBod against claims that it had incurred losses, saying documents he had reviewed showed otherwise. “I can tell you on authority that the Gold Board will relish any opportunity created for the issues that have come up over the period to be interrogated. So, they are ready. They are not running away from accountability,” he said. He said the Auditor-General’s 2025 report contained no adverse findings against GoldBod. “You have an auditor-general’s report dated 2025. No single adverse finding in that report was made against the Gold Board,” he said. Mr Agalga also cited an agreement between the PMMC and the Bank of Ghana covering costs associated with domestic gold purchases. He said those costs include “security, insurance, assay, smelting, etc.” According to him, GoldBod is an agent of the Bank of Ghana and therefore should not be treated as the entity bearing those costs. “The principal must pay the cost. Gold Board itself has never incurred losses. On the contrary, they have made a surplus, huge, in the region of what, 4 billion plus, thereabout, and that is captured in the Auditor-General’s report,” he said. Mr Agalga said the investigation should ultimately bring all the issues to the fore. “So let us bring all the issues to the fore, investigate the matters thoroughly, and whatever findings we make, the people of this country can be properly guided,” he said.

items.title: 3 more Adiala inmates seek private care
items.description: ISLAMABAD: At least three inma­tes of Adiala jail have approached the Isla­mabad High Court seeking treatment at private hospitals and greater access to their families, following the Supreme Court’s recent order directing authorities to shift former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital for medical examination and treatment. The petitions before the IHC vindicate the government’s concern that the SC order in Imran Khan’s case could set a precedent for other prisoners to seek similar relief. The federal government, in its review petition before the Supreme Court, had argued that allowing a convict to receive treatment at a private hospital could disturb the existing prison system and trigger a “floodgate” of similar applications from other prisoners. The issue is now before the IHC, where Justice Muhammad Asif sought comments from the jail superintendent on petitions filed by prisoners Ilyas Khan, Muhammad Ismail Khan and Owais Altaf. The court also issued noti­ces to prison authorities, and adjourned proceedings until Aug 27. During the hearing, Barrister Akhtar Chheena, representing Ismail Khan, said his client was suffering from haemophilia and had developed internal bleeding. He submitted that the prisoner had been taken to hospital around 10 times in the last two months, but his condition had not improved. According to the counsel, treatment for the particular condition was presently possible only at Shifa Interna­tio­nal Hospital. He relied upon the SC’s recent ruling and argued that where a disease could not be treated at a government hospital, a prisoner could be shifted to a private facility, with the family bearing the cost of treatment. The counsel requested the court to constitute a medical board to determine whether the required treatment was available at a government hospital. He questioned whether a prisoner should be denied access to a private facility if a necessary procedure, including a liver transplant, was not available at a government hospital. The petition filed by Owais Altaf was also pressed before Justice Muh­am­­mad Asif. His lawyer, Syed Jafar, ap­­p­eared through video link and submitted that the prisoner was suffering from fever and a heart ailment. He argued that receiving proper medical treatment was a fundamental right of a prisoner and maintained that the required treatment was not available at a government facility. The counsel consequently sought an order for Owais Altaf’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital for treatment. In another plea, Ismail Khan sought permission to communicate with his brother, who has been living in Dubai. The counsel requested that the jail authorities be directed to facilitate communication between the prisoner and his brother. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: L’administration américaine envisage d’annuler près de 200.000 visas d’affaires et tourismes dont les titulaires ont déposé par la suite des demandes d’asile
items.description: L'administration du président américain Donald Trump prévoit d'annuler jusqu'à 200 000 visas d'entrée délivrés à des étrangers titulaires de visas d'affaires ou de tourisme, après qu'ils aient déposé une demande d'asile aux États-Unis ou cherchent à obtenir l'asile, dans le cadre de la dernière escalade en date de la campagne menée par l'administration contre l'immigration. Un porte-parole du ministère des Affaires étrangères a déclaré que le ministère collaborait avec le ministère de la Sécurité intérieure afin d’identifier les titulaires de visas non immigrants qui sont entrés aux États-Unis en tant que visiteurs pour de courtes durées puis ont déposé une demande d’asile, en vue de l’annulation de leurs visas. Selon des documents du ministère des Affaires étrangères et des déclarations de responsables américains rapportées par l’agence Associated Press, cette campagne pourrait concerner les visas « B1 » et « B2 » délivrés entre 2016 et 2026. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères n’a pas précisé le nombre définitif de visas qui seront annulés. Le vice-ministre des Affaires étrangères, Christopher Landau, a déclaré sur la plateforme X que le système d’immigration américain était « submergé depuis longtemps par des demandes d’asile abusives ». Cette mesure s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une campagne plus large menée par l’administration Trump pour durcir les politiques d’immigration, qui a notamment consisté à annuler des visas et des cartes de résident permanent et à intensifier les expulsions. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères a indiqué avoir annulé plus de 175 000 visas depuis l’arrivée au pouvoir de Donald Trump. L’annulation de près de 200 000 visas, si elle est menée à bien à cette échelle, constituerait la plus grande annulation collective de visas de l’histoire des États-Unis, selon l’Associated Press.

items.title: Rawalpindi police chief rules out suicide in Hina Javaid’s death
items.description: RAWALPINDI: Regional Police Officer (RPO) Babar Sarfraz Alpa has disputed the impression that Hina Javaid’s death was a suicide. He categorically said “it was a murder”, adding her husband and a domestic servant are in police remand custody, while the father-in-law of the victim is under investigation. The RPO was speaking at a hurriedly-called joint press conference with City Police Officer Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, the SSP investigations and the SP Potohar at the Police Lines auditorium on Monday night. A special team has been formed to investigate the murder of digital media executive, Hina Javaid, 45. Says husband and servant in remand custody, father-in-law under probe Initially, it was portrayed as a suicide; however, after examining the body, the impression of suicide was ruled out. The victim’s father-in-law has been included in the investigation but has not been arrested. “The investigation into the case is at an early stage, so it is not appropriate to reveal certain things at this stage. However, as the investigation progresses, those who have played a role will be identified. As soon as concrete evidence is found against the victim’s father-in-law, action will be taken against him according to the law,” the RPO said. He said that on August 20, at 6am, Asghar Ali Fayyaz came to the police station and gave the initial information that thieves had broken into his house located on Faisal Alvi Road. He said on receiving the information, the police reached the spot where the body of Ms Javed was found in the bathroom of the apartment. “The body was tied to the shower and her hands were tied behind her back.” On the request of the deceased’s brother Fahad Javed, a case was registered under murder charges. The deceased’s husband Faisal Asghar Imam, father-in-law Asghar Fayyaz and domestic servant Zeeshan and an unknown person were named in the FIR. The RPO said that the investigation was being conducted from all angles and a special team had been formed under the leadership of the SSP investigations. He said the suspects, Zeeshan and Faisal, are in police custody. The RPO said all means, including technical and human intelligence, are being used in the investigation. The servant revealed to the investigating team that Faisal and Hina had a quarrel on the night of the incident over some issue during which she was reportedly tortured. As she tried to escape, she was strangled, he added. Later, she was taken to the bathroom to give an impression that she had committed suicide. The suspect had initially given a different statement but during the remand custody he made the disclosures. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: GoldBod has never incurred losses – Agalga challenges claims as Minority pushes probe
items.description: Incoming Majority Leader and Builsa North MP James Agalga has challenged claims that the Gold Board (GoldBod) incurred losses under its domestic gold purchasing operations. Speaking on Joy News’ P M Express on Monday, Mr Agalga said GoldBod itself had never incurred losses, insisting the institution had instead recorded a significant surplus. “Gold Board itself has never incurred losses. On the contrary, they have made a surplus, huge, in the region of what, 4 billion plus, thereabout, and that is captured in the Auditor-General’s report,” he said. His comments come amid a push by the Minority in Parliament for an ad hoc committee to investigate what it describes as losses from the government’s gold trading scheme. Mr Agalga said he had discussed the matter with GoldBod CEO Sammy Gyamfi and reviewed documents relevant to the debate. “And I can tell you on authority that the Gold Board will relish any opportunity created for the issues that have come up over the period to be interrogated,” he said. He added that GoldBod was “ready” and “not running away from accountability.” Mr Agalga also pointed to the 2025 Auditor-General’s report, arguing that it contained no adverse finding against GoldBod. “All the issues that have come up, okay, you have an auditor-general’s report dated 2025. No single adverse finding in that report was made against the Gold Board,” he said. He also cited an agreement dated 2023 between the now-defunct Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC) and the Bank of Ghana. According to him, the agreement contains provisions on costs associated with the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. He said the agreement remains in force and that transitional provisions made GoldBod the successor to PMMC, including responsibility for assets and liabilities. Mr Agalga said the agreement also makes clear that costs associated with gold purchases include security, insurance, assay and smelting. “Remember, the Gold Board is an agent of the Bank of Ghana. The principal must pay for the cost,” he said. He argued that the proposed parliamentary probe should therefore not be restricted to 2025. He said the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme began in 2021 and that Parliament must examine how gold purchases were handled under the previous administration. “Maybe what we need to do is probably to extend the scope of the probe,” he said. Mr Agalga cited an IMF report which, he said, indicated that $400 million was lost through the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. He explained that the programme was a deliberate government policy designed to support the cedi against the dollar. “It was a deliberate government policy, so we had to spend money. The Bank of Ghana had to spend money to achieve those objectives,” he said. He also questioned whether PMMC bought gold using forex bureau rates rather than Bank of Ghana rates in 2021, arguing that any differences between the rates could have created additional costs. He said Parliament should determine who bore those costs then and whether the same practice continues today. Mr Agalga warned that limiting the investigation to 2025 could undermine the process. “If you limit your investigation, when in actual fact we are talking about an agreement which is still in force and I have copies which hasn’t been terminated, it dates back to 2023, that agreement that I’ve seen between the Precious Minerals Marketing Company and the Bank of Ghana, which is still in force, and you limit the scope to only 2025, you’ll be doing a grave disservice to the people of this country,” he said. He called for a broader investigation to establish the full picture. “So let us bring all the issues to the fore, investigate the matters thoroughly, and whatever findings we make, the people of this country can be properly guided,” he said.

items.title: NAIMOS raids Ankobra, destroys 86 chanfang machines in fresh galamsey crackdown
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has intensified operations against illegal mining activities threatening the River Ankobra in the Western Region. The latest operation targeted illegal mining sites within the Ablebo General Area of the Ellembelle District. Three suspected illegal miners were arrested and handed over to the Police in Axim for further investigation. NAIMOS also destroyed several chanfang machines and water pumps found operating on the river. 86 Chanfang Machines Destroyed The River Ankobra is one of Ghana’s major water bodies that has suffered years of pollution from illegal mining. Since 2022, pollution levels in the river have worsened, with turbidity recorded in the thousands. Despite repeated raids, illegal miners continue to operate along sections of the river. NAIMOS has therefore intensified its operations to dismantle illegal mining sites and remove equipment from the waterway. So far, the operation has resulted in the destruction of 86 chanfang machines, 11 water pumps and two makeshift structures. With support from the Ghana Integrated Iron and Steel Development Corporation (GIISDEC), NAIMOS is also removing floating mining equipment for use as scrap. Operational commanders believe that destroying the equipment will significantly reduce illegal miners’ capacity to continue their activities in the affected areas. The operation is also expected to facilitate the removal of mining infrastructure from sections of the Ankobra River corridor.

items.title: Govt fails to maintain quorum as PPP stays away from National Assembly
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The ruling PML-N on Monday suffered an embarrassing setback in the National Assembly as the lower house was adjourned within minutes for lack of quorum after its estranged ally, the PPP, stayed away from the proceedings over the alleged rigging in the recently-held Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections. The government failed to muster the required number of 84 lawmakers in the 336-member house, forcing the chair to adjourn the session without taking up any agenda item when quorum was pointed out by an opposition member from the PTI. “No PPP, no quorum, simple,” posted PPP’s Sharmila Farooqui on her official social media account on X soon after the adjournment of the sitting. Later, Ms Farooqui told Dawn PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had already declared the party would “no more cooperate with PML-N on quorum and legislation” in the parliament till their grievances over the alleged rigging and mismanagement in the AJK polls were addressed. Sharmila says ‘no PPP, no quorum, simple’ Even those party MNAs who were present at the start of the Question Hour left the chamber immediately seeing only 20 to 25 PML-N members on the treasury benches, she said, adding that the PPP had been completing the quorum in the assembly previously. Ms Farooqui made it clear that the strategy would not change until their concerns over the AJK polls issue were addressed. She, however, did not elaborate any specific demand when asked as to what steps the party wanted the PML-N to take in order to allay their concerns when the election process had already been completed. When Speaker Ayaz Sadiq earlier announced the opening of the Question Hour, PTI’s Iqbal Afridi pointed out lack of quorum. His action came when the speaker refused him the floor to speak on a point of order. The speaker ordered a headcount and suspended the proceedings till the completion of the quorum. Some 35 minutes later, Deputy Speaker Ghulam Mustafa Shah was seen in the chair when the house resumed its proceedings. He adjourned the sitting till Tuesday after finding the house still not in order due to lack of quorum. While the PPP had supported the government in the passage of the two security-related bills last week, Mr Bhutto-Zardari, in the presence of PM Shehbaz Sharif, had objected to the manner with which the government had been doing legislation. After developing differences with the PML-N over the issue of AJK elections, a PPP delegation headed by Mr Bhutto-Zardari called on opposition leaders and sought their cooperation on the legislation in the parliament and its committees. Hina Javed’s murder At the outset of the sitting, the NA speaker expressed his concerns over the brutal murder of Hina Javed in Rawalpindi and referred the matter to the relevant house committee. Mr Sadiq disclosed that Hina Javed had been posted in the National Assembly by the National IT Board on attachment from December 2019 till June this year after which she returned to her parent department. He said though such matters generally fell under provincial jurisdiction, the case was of particular concern since she had served at the NA. He said the manner in which Hina Javed was murdered, and the violence against women, were matters of serious concern for everyone. He appreciated the Women Parliamentary Caucus for taking up the matter and said the NA would provide full support in monitoring the case and extending whatever assistance was required. Minister for Law and Human Rights Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ministry was in constant contact with the Rawalpindi police regarding the murder investigations. Two suspects were on three-day physical remand, he said, expressing the confidence that the culprits would be brought to justice. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.39, high-speed diesel by Rs2.40
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.39 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.40 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs341.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.69 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 25 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Amid distrust, Tehran wants US to initiate de-escalation
items.description: Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir exchanges views with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during their meeting in Tehran.—Reuters • CDF Munir holds meetings with Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf and Rezaei • Iranian leaders stress commitment to Islamabad MoU; say Washington’s approach hindering regional stability, eroding trust in US • Discussions focused on preventing further escalation, reopening of Hormuz, swift end to conflict, ISPR says • Oman FM due in Tehran today for next round of talks on Hormuz ISLAMABAD: The United States must take the first steps towards de-escalation by fulfilling its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), Iran conveyed to Pakistan on Monday, as the latter sought to revive the diplomatic process for ending the US-Iran conflict. The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s meetings in Tehran; with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Gen Mohsen Rezaei, as he sounded out Tehran on the possibility of reviving the June understanding. “We are committed to implementing the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding. It is the United States that must adhere to its commitments based on the agreement,” Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir, according to an Iranian account of their meeting. This sentiment was echoed by Gen Rezaei in his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, who was quoted by IRNA as saying: “We distrust America and it must change its behaviour”. Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported. According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accompanied the army chief during the one-day visit, which also included meetings with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. “Comprehensive discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and expedited termination of the conflict. The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the ways to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the disputes,” ISPR said. The Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and sincere efforts towards facilitating dialogue, de-escalation and a peaceful resolution of the conflict, the statement noted. The field marshal’s visit comes as the two warring sides have returned to hostilities following the expiry of the 60-day armistice brokered under the Islamabad MoU. Pakistan has, however, continued to regard the agreement as the available framework for a return to dialogue, while Iran has insisted that Washington must first address what Tehran considers breaches of the understanding. The visit assumes added significance because Field Marshal Munir spoke by telephone with US President Donald Trump last week, before travelling to Tehran. The contents of that conversation have not been made public, but the contact provided Islamabad with a direct channel to carry the US position to Tehran, while seeking to assess whether Iran was prepared to re-engage. The army chief’s trip began just before Washington announced a fresh economic pressure campaign against Iran, with sanctions and restrictions on Iranian oil exports likely to form a major part of the new measures. Tehran has warned that further US pressure would deepen the confrontation rather than create conditions for negotiations. Ghalibaf described Washington’s approach as “hinder[ing] regional stability and further erod[ing] trust in Washington”. “Americans know that no one buys their bombast, the United States is not in an economic position to further restrict its relations with other countries,” he said in a post on X after meeting Field Marshal Munir. The Strait of Hormuz remains central to the impasse. Iran has been insisting that US first fulfil its commitments relating to the waterway, before it considers a wider reopening and a return to the next phase of negotiations. Field Marshal Munir’s meeting with Gen Rezaei was particularly significant because the Iranian general has recently taken over as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, placing him at the centre of Tehran’s national security decision making at this critical stage in its confrontation with Washington. During their conversation, Rezaei particularly emphasised Iran’s security interests in the Strait of Hormuz and the need for any settlement to address the military and economic pressures imposed on Tehran. The issue of Strait of Hormuz is meanwhile being discussed in a separate diplomatic track in the shape of Iran-Oman talks on arrangements for navigation in the strait. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Al Busaidi is due in Tehran on Tuesday, adding to the diplomatic activity surrounding the strait at a time when Pakistan is seeking to regain its role in the wider US-Iran process. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: FBR eases sales tax registration for businesses
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has announced new measures to streamline sales tax registration for businesses, particularly those considered low risk. Under the new system, applications filed through the IRIS portal will be screened using risk-based checks. The measures were notified through Sales Tax General Order No. 20 of 2026, issued on Monday. Under the new procedures, applicants falling in the low-risk category will be processed within three working days under a risk-based framework, provided all required documents are complete. Applications will be submitted through the computerised IRIS system. The FBR has directed all field formations not to demand additional documents unless they are legally required or flagged by the risk-based system. Bars field offices from seeking unnecessary documents To further facilitate manufacturers, the FBR has asked sectoral associations under the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry to issue pre-registration certificates to their members. These certificates will confirm that the applicant is engaged in manufacturing, that the business premises are identifiable, that the activity corresponds with the relevant sector and that the details provided match the association’s records. The certificates will be sent electronically to the local registration office (LRO) along with other required documents. The FBR clarified that these certificates are intended only to expedite verification and do not replace legal requirements or grant any exemptions. It also pointed out that associations will be held responsible if false information is discovered during physical checks. Local registration offices must also conduct on-site verification of manufacturers within three working days. At the same time, the FBR stressed that applications flagged as high-risk will continue to face stricter scrutiny, including pre- and post-verification. Even low-risk registrations may be rechecked later if irregularities are detected. To make the registration process quicker and more transparent, the FBR has laid out a step-by-step procedure. All applications filed through the IRIS portal will be screened using a risk-based system. Those identified as low-risk will be given priority and, if complete, processed within three working days. Field formations have been instructed not to ask for additional documents unless they are legally required, needed to verify information or flagged by the computerised risk system. If an application is incomplete, the applicant must be informed within seven days, with clear details of what is missing, what needs to be corrected and how much time is allowed to rectify the deficiencies. The order also directs that no vague or general objections be raised — every objection must be specific and linked to a clear requirement. Once the missing information is provided, the application should proceed without requiring the applicant to restart the process. Published in Dawn, August 25th, 2026

items.title: Trump administration moves to impose more than $100,000 fee for H-1B worker visas
items.description: President Donald Trump ‘s administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented fee of more than $100,000 on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, a measure that has been blocked by the courts. The fee, first temporarily imposed by Trump last year, dramatically raises the cost of visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education, and research sectors. A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while another court considers whether a judge properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group. Trump’s temporary fee increase expires in September, one year after it was issued. ​The proposed rule by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, posted in the Federal Register on Monday, would make a ⁠$103,265 fee permanent. It could be finalised by the end of the year. The H-1B program allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers with training in speciality fields and offers 65,000 visas annually, with an additional 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years. Those visas typically carried fees of $2,000 to $5,000 before Trump’s order. The fee would not apply to visas granted to foreign citizens already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of new H-1B recipients, or to renewals of current visas. DEBATE OVER VISA PROGRAM Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B program say it is abused by many companies that replace ​American workers with cheaper foreign labour. But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa program is needed to address a shortage of qualified American workers for certain jobs and to allow U.S. businesses to recruit top talent. About 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee on a total of 85 visa applications as ‌of late ⁠February, according to court filings. In imposing the fee, Trump invoked the president’s authority under immigration law to restrict the entry of certain foreign nationals deemed detrimental to U.S. interests. The fee is being challenged by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce , the largest U.S. business lobbying group, Democratic-led states and a coalition of unions and employers. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the rule proposed this week once it is finalised. LEGAL CHALLENGES MOUNT The lawsuits claim that Trump’s power to restrict entry does not allow him to override the law that created the H-1B visa program. The states and groups that sued also say that the Department of Homeland Security cannot impose fees, taxes, or other means of generating revenue for the United States without permission from Congress. The Trump administration has maintained that the fee is not a traditional tax and that courts have little power to question the president’s authority to restrict entry into the country. Amid Trump’s broader immigration crackdown, employers last year registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas, down more than 25% from 2024 and to fewer than half of the 794,000 visas sought in 2023, according to data from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. The Trump administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed a new ⁠visa selection ​process that would favour higher-skilled and better-paid workers. Earlier in August, the Department of Homeland ​Security, in a separate rule, added fees of up to $4,500 to applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or to transfer employees based in other countries to the United States.
